text: え　なんだい　それは　わしに　くれるっての　かい？

structure.jp: わしに　くれるっての　かい？
structure.en: you mean you're giving it to me?

patterns.name: 〜という
patterns.explanation: っての is the casual squeezed form of というの, 'the thing you are saying'. It is used to check what the other person means. くれるっての = 'you're saying you'll give it'.

patterns.name: 〜かい
patterns.span: くれるっての　かい
patterns.explanation: かい is a soft, casual way to ask a yes-or-no question, mostly used by older men. くれるってのかい = 'you mean you're giving it?'

patterns.name: 〜だい
patterns.explanation: だい at the end makes a friendly, casual question that goes with a question word. なんだい = 'what is it?'
